newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open barely changed Tuesday, dealers said.

The funds could stage a run for the new contract highs reached on Monday in an attempt to push the benchmark October contract over 10.72 cents. But producer selling is likely to slow gains, they added, pegging resistance at each point up.

Monday, October ended up 0.07 cent at 11.70 cents a lb after trading from a lifetime high of 11.72 cents to 11.60 cents. Second-position March finished 0.05 cent firmer at 11.95 cents, while the rest settled 0.04 to 0.06 higher.
An estimated 15,454 lots changed hands on the day.

In fundamental news, the average sugar content of beet in southern Spain tested at 17.2 percent on July 27, the National Sugar Beet Association said. The southern harvest has yielded a crop of 1.43 million tonnes at an average sugar content of 17.2 percent.
LIFFE white sugar futures were down slightly on Tuesday following the higher close on Monday. At 0850 EDT/1250 GMT, October stood 10 cents lower at $329.70.
